searchText: In Teku we consider the EL to be offline when we get connection errors (when establishing a web socket connection and get errors, not when getting json RPC error responses which means that the EL is online but the requests are failing for other reasons) Do most clients do polling for remote signer keys provided via URL? i heard nimbus and lodestar does maybe <@586161934425128960> might know yeah we do fetch pubkeys initially on startup and then once a epoch, Nimbus does something similar as well afaik I don't know of any other client that does it at the start of the epoch or somewhere in the middle when there's less stuff going on acutally it's not epoch aligned because it is configurable and any ms value could be set, the default value is just once an epoch but more like once every ~6.4 minutes gotcha still debating if we should have something like this i'm kinda afraid of adding a feature like this for our current setup might need more refactorings alternative would be to just use the keymanager api, which is what eth-docker does to keep keys in sync yeah that's why i'm hesitant will investigate this a bit more btw (different topic) was anything decided on event api stuff for electra? circling back to beacon API work as soon as I wrap up builder stuff dappnode does it as well like this, I've only heard from Diva so far regarding this feature I don't think we want a v2 and skeptical if we even need versioned topics for attestation and attester slashing but open for anything if teams prefer it one way or the other, we have just implemented it currently to extract the slot and determine the fork type that way have any of you talked to major consumers? I can't think of anyone who would listen to attestation events but for attester slashing there are a few solutions and validator clients that use them to stop operations if any of the imported keys are slashed

excerpts.author: mehdi.aouadi
excerpts.content: In Teku we consider the EL to be offline when we get connection errors (when establishing a web socket connection and get errors, not when getting json RPC error responses which means that the EL is online but the requests are failing for other reasons)

excerpts.author: jameshe5018
excerpts.content: Do most clients do polling for remote signer keys provided via URL? i heard nimbus and lodestar does maybe <@586161934425128960> might know

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: yeah we do fetch pubkeys initially on startup and then once a epoch, Nimbus does something similar as well afaik

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: I don't know of any other client that does it

excerpts.author: jameshe5018
excerpts.content: at the start of the epoch or somewhere in the middle when there's less stuff going on

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: acutally it's not epoch aligned because it is configurable and any ms value could be set, the default value is just once an epoch but more like once every ~6.4 minutes

excerpts.author: jameshe5018
excerpts.content: still debating if we should have something like this i'm kinda afraid of adding a feature like this for our current setup

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: alternative would be to just use the keymanager api, which is what eth-docker does to keep keys in sync

excerpts.content: yeah that's why i'm hesitant will investigate this a bit more
